items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (ShopEngine, requestAfterSale, refundFormItems) and the formatting is consistent. But business logic has few comments, and the event-wiring block is long with terse names (`res`, `e`, `self`). round2 adds Number.EPSILON with no explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new file of about 1920 lines (cap: at most accept). The event-binding method that wires every button in the UI (pay/ship/cancel/aftersale/refund/confirm modal) runs well over 100 lines. ShopEngine mixes UI state (activeTab, showCheckoutModal) with domain logic in one class.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: API methods return {ok:false,error} and the UI shows those errors as toasts. However, quantity inputs use `parseInt(e.target.value) || 0`, which silently turns bad input into 0. Magic numbers like the 9折 member rate and hard-coded rounding are scattered through the code. Every hidden test failed, including the basic ones.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Only cancel goes through confirmModalData. btn-submit-refund calls requestAfterSale directly, and btn-confirm-return calls confirmReturn directly, with no confirmation. No confirmation is visible for import or reset. The order cards have status badges and per-status buttons, and the cart has a summary area.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: window.shopTestAPI delegates to the same engine methods the UI uses, which is good. But money is float arithmetic with round2 (`Math.round((val+EPSILON)*100)/100`), not integer cents. Seed amounts like 66.47 are hard-coded. Import validation is not visible, and the hidden tests all failed.
